title: fix(cloud-workers): first turn after a Gateway update fails with a missing worker bundle
body:
Related: #160730

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Gateway update, a cloud worker's first turn could fail with `ENOENT ... realpath '<node-host>/gateway-<ns>/bundles/<bundleHash>'` because node cleanup deleted the worker bundle the in-place runtime refresh had just installed.

## User Impact

User impact: cloud machines that are refreshed in place after a Gateway update, and cold-provisioned machines, keep the newly installed worker bundle until the environment records it, so the next turn launches instead of failing with a missing bundle.

## Why This Change Was Made

#160730 fixed this failure for cold provisioning and explicitly left runtime refresh open. Refresh has the same window: `provider-runtime-refresh.ts` installs the new bundle, then records the new receipt afterwards (`store.refreshBootstrapReceipt`). Throughout that window the environment stays `ready`/`idle`/`attached` with its old receipt.

The node marks each finished install with a new generation. It protects that bundle only until the Gateway acknowledges the generation, and the Gateway acknowledges whatever generation the previous retain pass returned. A retain pass that the node queues behind the install (its per-namespace queue serializes them) returns the new generation, even though the Gateway built its keep set from the old receipt. The next pass then prunes the refreshed bundle.

This is reachable after every Gateway update. The node reconnects, and its first retain pass lands behind the refresh install. The first bundle-status acceptance on a new connection (`undefined -> installed`) reschedules the same node, so a second pass races the receipt write. The 60 s placement reconcile and node inventory changes can also supply that pass during long installs.

Persistent hosts were already safe because the coordinator always pins the Gateway's current build there. Environment-owned cloud nodes were deliberately excluded from that pin (#140449), so they were exposed.

Provisioning and refresh share one cause: both install the Gateway's current build (the same memoized `prepareInstallation("bundle")` artifact that `bundleRetention.currentBuild()` returns) before recording it. The retain coordinator now applies one rule: **keep the current build on a node until every live environment there has recorded it.** This completes the reachability snapshot instead of suspending retention, and it replaces the provisioning-only `bundleRetentionReady` special case from #160730. Pruning of other bundles continues during provisioning and refresh.

If preparing the current build fails, the coordinator now sends a workspace-only retain request (no bundle keep set, generation acknowledgement or status query) and warns. Workspace retention on cloud nodes therefore still does not depend on bundle preparation; this addresses ClawSweeper's P2 on the first head.

Other behavior is unchanged:
- Persistent hosts keep their existing always-on pin and status target.
- Cloud nodes still report their environment receipt as bundle status.
- The status pin appears only while an environment is converging.
- Cloud nodes now resolve `currentBuild()` when bundle retention is supported. The provider reconcile loop already prepares that artifact for every ready, idle or attached environment.
- No protocol, schema, store or lifecycle changes.

## Evidence

- The regression in `src/node-host/node-worker-bundle-installer.test.ts` extends the #160730 pattern to two phases: cold provisioning and runtime refresh. It uses the real node installer, the real retain coordinator, a queued retain pass during the install, receipt recording and the real launch-path resolver.
  - On the previous coordinator, the runtime-refresh phase fails with the live error: `ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath '.../gateway-test/bundles/8450792f...'`. The provisioning phase passes, as expected with #160730 in place.
  - With the fix, both phases pass. The refresh phase also proves that the previous bundle is pruned once the new receipt is recorded, so retention still works rather than being suspended.
- A coordinator unit test covers the rule on a cloud node:
  - a stale receipt pins the current build, and the status target stays the receipt;
  - once the receipt records the current build, only that hash is kept;
  - once the environment is terminal, nothing is pinned.
- Test results:
  - `node-worker-bundle-installer.test.ts`: 27/27 pass.
  - `node-workspace-retain-coordinator.test.ts`: 20/20 pass.
  - `server-worker-placement-startup-maintenance.test.ts`: 7/7 pass.
- Measured cost (`--maxWorkers=1`, verbose reporter):
  - new runtime-refresh case: 686 ms (the existing provisioning case is 614 ms);
  - new coordinator test: 3 ms;
  - no timers, sleeps or new fixtures.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` on the touched files passed conflict markers, line-cap/max-lines/assertion ratchets, format, plugin boundaries, wrapper shadowing, core tsgo graph boundary and core typecheck.
  - `typecheck core tests` failed only in untouched `ui/src/components/*` files, because this worktree has a gateway-only install without UI packages (`@panzoom/panzoom`, `@modelcontextprotocol/client`) and resolves `@types/markdown-it` from a parent checkout.
  - The test graphs for the touched files passed in a separate run.
  - `oxlint` and `oxfmt` on the touched files are clean.
- Codex autoreview (P2 threshold, with the refresh, provisioning, installer and retention sources as evidence) is scoped-clean on the first head. After merging main and adding the preparation-failure fallback, the full-candidate review reported only the committed-state gap that the fallback commit closes.
- Merged main (merge commit, no rebase). Only the coordinator conflicted: main's async manifest-ref preparation, terminal-state helper and per-dispatch recheck are kept, and the bundle snapshot is taken after the last preparation await.
- Post-merge results: coordinator 26/26 and installer 27/27 pass; maintenance 7/7 passes; `pnpm tsgo:core`, targeted oxlint, oxfmt, `git diff --check` and the touched test-graph typecheck shards pass. The new preparation-failure regression takes 40 ms and failed before the fallback.
- The first head's CI failure (`checks-node-changed-compact-large-15-2`) is unrelated to this change. `src/gateway/server.agent.rpc-contracts.test.ts` failed in `beforeAll` Gateway startup (`Startup failed: required secrets are unavailable ... Shared-state worker opening path changed`, `STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED`). The preceding file in the same Vitest worker had just retired the shared-state worker owner. This PR touches no state-database, secrets or startup code.
- The second head's CI failures were main-side test defects that #161455 has since fixed. `checks-node-changed-compact-small-7-3` failed in `src/cron/service.failure-alert-notifications.test.ts` and `src/cron/service.heartbeat-busy-poll.test.ts`. `checks-node-changed-compact-small-3-1` failed in `src/infra/update-candidate-canary.test.ts` (streamed candidate progress). Locally the cron suites passed and the canary failure reproduced on the merged main content, which this PR does not touch. I merged current main (clean merge, PR diff unchanged) to pick up that fix.
- The earlier `server.agent.rpc-contracts.test.ts` startup failure did not recur on the second head. A local two-file replay in the CI order failed both Gateway suites in this gateway-only worktree install. I did not capture enough output to tell that apart from the environment, so the cause is unconfirmed and I claim no fix here.
- Not run: a live cold-Hetzner or in-place-update cell. The regression reproduces the exact live `ENOENT` at the installer–coordinator boundary.
